tool_input.command: bun run console posts:scheduled; echo "exit=$?"; bun run console list 2>/dev/null | head -40
tool_input.description: Run the console with an unknown command to see baseline output

result:
Scheduled publishing is implemented. `bun run typecheck` passes and `bun test` passes (21 tests, 19 of them new); lint and `bunx guren check` are clean too. I left the changes uncommitted in the working tree.

Decisions you may want to revisit:

- **Home page shows public posts only**, even to the author. Their scheduled posts appear in the posts list, as the request asks; the home page wasn't mentioned, and it would otherwise have leaked scheduled posts.
- **Edit, update and delete also answer 404** for a scheduled post when the viewer is not its author. A 403 would have confirmed the post exists. Public posts still answer 403 to non-authors, as today.
- **`publishAt` must carry a zone** (`Z` or an offset). A bare local time like `2999-01-01T09:00` is rejected, because the server would otherwise read it in its own zone. The form converts the browser's local time to UTC before sending.
- **A `PUT` without `publishAt` clears the date**, per the contract. The edit form sends the current date back so an untouched edit doesn't publish a scheduled post.
- **Timestamps are compared as text.** A `published_at` written by hand in another format (no milliseconds, a space instead of `T`) can compare wrongly when it falls on the same day as now.
- **The report replaces tabs and line breaks in a title with a space**, so one post is always one line with three fields.
- **Each post carries an extra `scheduled` boolean** next to `publishedAt`, decided on the server so pages don't rely on the visitor's clock.

The report reads whichever database the environment selects, so checking the test database means running it as `env NODE_ENV=test bun run console posts:scheduled`. I ran it that way against hand-inserted rows: stdout held only the rows, soonest first.

**Summary of changes:** I added the nullable `publishedAt` / `published_at` column in `db/schema.ts` with a generated migration in `db/migrations/20260929173228_add_published_at_to_posts/`. `app/Models/Post.ts` now holds the visibility rule (`Post.visibleTo()`, a `scheduled` scope, `Post.isScheduled()`), and `PostController.ts` and `HomeController.ts` read through it. `PostValidator.ts` validates and normalises `publishAt`, `PostResource.ts` exposes `publishedAt` and `scheduled`, and `PostPolicy.ts` states the same view rule. The report is `app/Console/Commands/PostsScheduledCommand.ts`, registered in `src/console.ts`. On the front end, a shared `resources/js/components/PublishAtField.tsx` is used by `posts/New.tsx` and `posts/Edit.tsx`, and `posts/Index.tsx` and `posts/Show.tsx` show a "Scheduled · goes live …" line. I also regenerated the `.guren/*.gen.ts` files, added `tests/ScheduledPosts.test.ts`, and recorded the decision in `docs/adr/0002-scheduled-posts-become-public-at-read-time.md`.
